newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Nafta sees SKK 1bln in investments.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Nafta sees SKK 1bln in investments.

text.p: Nafta Gbely a.s., Slovakia's monopoly oil and gas storage company, on Wednesday said it would invest up to one billion crowns in the next eight years to expand its activities.

"There are four major investment plans for which the total investment will be one billion crowns over the next eight years," spokesman Kozef Lacko told journalists after an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.
* Doubling the present gas storage capacities from two to four billion cubic metres.
* Increasing natural gas production from its own Slovak resources.
* Launching crude oil production in Kazakhstan under a joint-venture with the Kazakh company, Anacon.
Slovakia consumes an average 30-32 million cubic metres of natural gas a day. Nafta's current storage capacity is sufficient to cover some two-thirds of the country's gas consumption.

The state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), in August sold its entire holdings in Nafta to little known private company Druha Obchodna for 500 million crowns, far below its market value of about 3.2 billion crowns.
The sell-off raised eyebrows since at the time of the sale, Nafta shares stood at around 2,000 crowns while the NPF sale price averaged about 400 crowns a share.
